pages.summary: Points in time, as values that print, compare and add as dates.
body: A datetime holds a date and time of day, with a display format and, if given, a time zone. It is made from years, months, days (and hours, minutes, seconds), from text, or from numbers of another kind (`'ConvertFrom'`): serial date numbers, POSIX seconds, Excel day numbers, Julian dates or yyyymmdd numbers. Datetimes compare and sort as times; subtracting two gives a duration, adding a duration or a calendarDuration gives another datetime, and a number adds days. The parts read and set as properties (`t.Year`, `t.Month`, `t.Day`, `t.Hour`, `t.Minute`, `t.Second`), and `t.Format` and `t.TimeZone` change the display and the zone. A zoned datetime follows the zone's summer time.
syntax: t = datetime(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)
With a display format and a time zone.

examples.title: Made, formatted, compared and subtracted
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 0)
t.Format = 'eeee d MMMM yyyy, HH:mm'
u = datetime('2026-12-24 18:00', 'InputFormat', 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm');
u > t
u - t
t + 1.5
examples.output:
t = 

  datetime

   05-Nov-2026 14:30:00

t = 

  datetime

   Thursday 5 November 2026, 14:30

ans =

  logical

   1

ans = 

  duration

   1179:30:00

ans = 

  datetime

   Saturday 7 November 2026, 02:30

examples.title: The clocks put forward in spring
examples.intro: In Stockholm the clocks went from 02:00 to 03:00 on 29 March 2026, so an hour after half past one is half past three.

notes: Formats are letters: `uuuu` or `yyyy` for the year, `MM`, `MMM` and `MMMM` for the month as a number, a short and a full name, `dd` for the day, `eee` and `eeee` for the weekday's name, `HH` for the hour (`hh` with `a` for a 12-hour clock), `mm` for minutes, `ss` for seconds and `SSS` for their fraction. Text in single quotes is kept as it is, as in `'yyyy-MM-dd''T''HH:mm'`.

pages.summary: Not-a-Time, the missing datetime; and tests for datetimes and missing ones.
body: `NaT` is a missing datetime, as NaN is a missing number: comparisons with it are false, and it sorts last. Text that reads as no date becomes NaT. `isnat` is true where a datetime is NaT, `isdatetime` for a datetime at all.

examples.title: A missing date among others
examples.code:
t = [datetime(2026, 1, 1) NaT datetime(2026, 3, 1)]
isnat(t)
t(2) == t(2)
sort(t, 'descend')
[isdatetime(t), isdatetime(738000)]
examples.output:
t = 

  1×3 datetime array

   01-Jan-2026   NaT   01-Mar-2026

ans =

  1×3 logical array

   0   1   0

ans =

  logical

   0

ans = 

  1×3 datetime array

   NaT   01-Mar-2026   01-Jan-2026

ans =

  1×2 logical array

   1   0

pages.summary: The parts of datetimes, as numbers or names.
body: Each gives an array of the size of the datetimes: the year, the quarter (1 to 4), the month (or its `'name'` or `'shortname'`), the week of the year (from the week holding 1 January, weeks starting on Sunday) or of the month, the day of the month (or of the week, 1 for Sunday, or of the year, or its name), the hour, the minute, and the second with its fraction. For a NaT each is NaN.
syntax: The week of the year; week(t, 'weekofmonth') of the month.

examples.title: A Saturday in February taken apart
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 2, 14, 9, 5, 30.25);
[year(t) quarter(t) month(t) day(t)]
[week(t) week(t, 'weekofmonth') day(t, 'dayofweek') day(t, 'dayofyear')]
[hour(t) minute(t)]
second(t)
month(t, 'name')
day(t, 'name')
examples.output:
ans =

        2026           1           2          14

ans =

     7     2     7    45

ans =

     9     5

ans =

   30.2500

ans = 

  1×1 cell array

    {'February'}

ans = 

  1×1 cell array

    {'Saturday'}

pages.summary: The year, month and day, and the hour, minute and second, of datetimes; the time since midnight.
body: `ymd` gives the date's three parts, `hms` the time's (for durations too, as hours, minutes and seconds), and `timeofday` the time since midnight as a duration, so that `t - timeofday(t)` is the day's start.
syntax: The time's parts, of a datetime or a duration.

examples.title: A date and a time of day
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 11, 5, 14, 30, 15);
[y, m, d] = ymd(t)
[h, mi, s] = hms(t)
timeofday(t)
[h, mi, s] = hms(duration(26, 5, 0))

pages.summary: Datetimes on a weekend, and between two others.
body: `isweekend` is true on Saturdays and Sundays; `isbetween` where a datetime lies between a lower and an upper one, the ends included, or (with `'open'`, `'openleft'` or `'openright'`) left out.
syntax: True between them, the ends included.
With the ends included or left out.

examples.title: A week, its weekend and its middle
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 11, 1:7);
isweekend(t)
isbetween(t, datetime(2026, 11, 3), datetime(2026, 11, 5))
isbetween(t, datetime(2026, 11, 3), datetime(2026, 11, 5), 'open')
examples.output:
ans =

  1×7 logical array

   1   0   0   0   0   0   1

ans =

  1×7 logical array

   0   0   1   1   1   0   0

ans =

  1×7 logical array

   0   0   0   1   0   0   0

pages.summary: Datetimes as numbers of other kinds.
body: `posixtime` gives seconds since 1 January 1970 (UTC for zoned datetimes); `juliandate` days since noon on 1 January 4713 BC (or, `'modifiedjuliandate'`, since midnight on 17 November 1858); `exceltime` Excel's day number (from 1900, or 1904). `convertTo` gives any of these, and `'datenum'`, `'yyyymmdd'`, or ticks from an epoch of one's own. `datetime(X, 'ConvertFrom', kind)` goes back.

examples.title: The first of January 2026 as numbers
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 1, 1);
format long g
posixtime(t)
juliandate(t)
juliandate(t, 'modifiedjuliandate')
exceltime(t)
convertTo(t, 'yyyymmdd')
convertTo(t, 'epochtime', 'Epoch', datetime(2026, 1, 1), 'TicksPerSecond', 1000)
datetime(46023, 'ConvertFrom', 'excel')

pages.summary: The offset of a datetime's time zone from UTC.
body: A duration for each datetime: the zone's offset at that moment, summer time included (and 0 for a datetime without a zone). The second output is the summer-time part alone.

examples.title: Winter and summer in Stockholm
examples.output:
d = 

  1×2 duration array

   01:00:00   02:00:00

dst = 

  1×2 duration array

   00:00:00   01:00:00

pages.summary: Datetimes moved to the start or end of a unit of time, or to a day of the week.
body: `'start'` moves to the start of the year, quarter, month, week (Sunday), day, hour, minute or second that holds the datetime; `'end'` to its end: the last day of a week, month, quarter or year, and the next start of a day, hour, minute or second. A rule moves to that unit `'next'`, `'previous'`, or a number of units away first. `'dayofweek'` moves to a day of the week (a name, or 1 for Sunday to 7), the next one unless the rule says `'previous'`, `'nearest'` or `'current'`.
syntax: Of a unit before or after.
To a day of the week.

examples.title: Around a Saturday in February
examples.code:
t = datetime(2026, 2, 14, 9, 5, 30)
dateshift(t, 'start', 'month')
dateshift(t, 'end', 'month')
dateshift(t, 'start', 'month', 'next')
dateshift(t, 'start', 'week')
dateshift(t, 'dayofweek', 'Friday')

ans =

examples.title: The last day of each month of a year

body: `between` gives the difference from t1 to t2 as a calendarDuration of years, months, days and time (or the components asked for); added to t1 it gives t2. `caldiff` gives the differences between consecutive datetimes. Subtracting datetimes gives a duration instead, an exact length of time.
syntax: In years, months, days and time.

examples.title: A stay measured three ways
examples.code:
a = datetime(2026, 1, 15);
b = datetime(2027, 3, 20);
d = between(a, b)
a + d == b
between(a, b, 'days')
b - a
caldiff(datetime(2026, [1 3 4], 15))
examples.output:
d = 

  calendarDuration

   1y 2mo 5d

ans =

  logical

   1

ans = 

  calendarDuration

   429d

ans = 

  duration

   10296:00:00

ans = 

  1×2 calendarDuration array

   2mo   1mo

pages.summary: Lengths of time: exact amounts of hours, minutes and seconds.
body: A duration is made from hours, minutes and seconds (and milliseconds), or from text. Durations add, subtract, scale and compare; subtracting datetimes gives one. The format sets the display: a clock form (`'hh:mm:ss'`, `'dd:hh:mm:ss'`, `'hh:mm'`, `'mm:ss'`, each with `.SSS` for fractions), or one unit (`'y'`, `'d'`, `'h'`, `'m'`, `'s'`). `hours`, `minutes` and the like give a duration as a number.

examples.title: Laps added up
examples.code:
laps = duration(0, [4 4 3], [52 38.5 59.5], 'Format', 'mm:ss.SSS')
total = sum(laps)
mean(laps)
total.Format = 's'
isduration(total)
examples.output:
laps = 

  1×3 duration array

   04:52.000   04:38.500   03:59.500

total = 

  duration

   13:30.000

ans = 

  duration

   04:30.000

total = 

  duration

   810 sec

ans =

  logical

   1

examples.title: Durations from text, compared

pages.summary: Durations of a unit, and durations as numbers of that unit.
body: Given numbers, each makes durations of that unit (a year is 365.2425 days, the mean of the calendar); given durations, it gives their length in that unit. For calendar lengths that depend on where they start, use `calyears`, `calmonths`, `caldays` and the like.

examples.title: Units made and converted
examples.code:
d = hours([1 2.5 30])
minutes(d)
days(hours(36))
days(years(1))
seconds(milliseconds(1500))
examples.output:
d = 

  1×3 duration array

   1 hr   2.5 hr   30 hr

ans =

          60         150        1800

ans =

    1.5000

ans =

  365.2425

ans =

    1.5000

examples.title: Durations as the axis of a plot

pages.summary: Lengths of time in calendar units, whose length depends on where they start.
body: A calendarDuration holds months (a year is 12, a quarter 3), days (a week is 7) and a time. Added to a datetime, a month is the same day of the next month (the last day if the month is shorter) and a day is the same time of the next day, however long it is. `between` gives one from two datetimes; `split` takes one apart.
syntax: c = calendarDuration(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)

examples.title: Months that are not all the same length
examples.code:
c = calendarDuration(1, 2, 3)
t = datetime(2026, 1, 31);
t + calmonths(1)
t + days(31)
datetime(2024, 2, 29) + calyears(1)
examples.output:
c = 

  calendarDuration

   1y 2mo 3d

ans = 

  datetime

   28-Feb-2026

ans = 

  datetime

   03-Mar-2026

ans = 

  datetime

   28-Feb-2025
